name: Baricitinib
lead: Baricitinib (brand name Olumiant) is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) 1 and 2 inhibitor developed by Incyte and Eli Lilly and approved for rheumatoid arthritis, severe alopecia areata and hospitalised COVID-19 [1]. For hair, it is relevant to alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition causing patchy or total hair loss, rather than to common male pattern baldness [2][3].

In June 2022 the FDA approved baricitinib as the first systemic treatment for severe alopecia areata in adults, based on the BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 phase 3 trials [1][4]. A European consensus statement notes that baricitinib and ritlecitinib are the only two EMA-approved medications for alopecia areata [2].

It carries a boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis [1]. No community discussion of baricitinib for appearance was found in forum sources; it is included as a medically relevant hair-loss drug.

paras: Baricitinib is indicated for moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis after inadequate response to TNF antagonists, for severe alopecia areata, and for hospitalised adults with COVID-19 requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilation [1]. It has also been studied in atopic dermatitis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis and vitiligo [5][6][7], and JAK inhibitors for rheumatoid arthritis are reviewed [8].

A European consensus defines a SALT score of 20 or higher as a commonly accepted indication for systemic therapy in alopecia areata, and lists baricitinib for adults among two EMA-approved options, with glucocorticoids, cyclosporine, methotrexate and azathioprine used off-label [2]. The FDA approval in June 2022 applies to adults with at least 50 percent scalp hair loss (SALT 50 or higher) lasting more than six months [1].

The BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 phase 3 randomised trials, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2022, compared baricitinib 2 mg and 4 mg with placebo in adults with severe alopecia areata; a larger proportion of participants on 4 mg achieved a SALT score of 20 or lower at week 36 than on placebo [4]. A later analysis from BRAVE-AA1 examined withdrawal and retreatment in patients with severe disease [9]. A short commentary on baricitinib for alopecia areata was also published [10].

The boxed warning covers serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis, with screening for tuberculosis and monitoring of blood counts, lipids and liver enzymes [1]. Common effects include upper respiratory infections, headache, nausea and raised cholesterol, and live vaccines are contraindicated [1].

Baricitinib competitively inhibits JAK1 and JAK2 enzymes, disrupting JAK-STAT signalling by which several inflammatory cytokines act, including in joints, skin and hair follicles [1]. Alopecia areata is understood as an immune attack on hair follicles, which is the rationale for JAK inhibition [2].

Baricitinib was approved by the FDA on 31 May 2018 for rheumatoid arthritis, emergency use for COVID-19 followed on 19 November 2020 with full approval on 11 May 2022, and the alopecia areata approval came in June 2022 [1]. Its COVID-19 benefit was evaluated in the RECOVERY platform trial and in animal models [11][12].

Phase 3 evidence for alopecia areata comes from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 [4], with a withdrawal and retreatment analysis [9]. Registered trials include a phase 2 study in central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia in adults of African descent [13]. Studies in other conditions include rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, atopic dermatitis and vitiligo [5][6][7][14]. No trials of baricitinib in common male or female pattern hair loss were identified.

timeline.event: FDA approves baricitinib for rheumatoid arthritis [1].
BRAVE-AA trials published; FDA approves it for severe alopecia areata [1][4].

card.summary: A prescription JAK inhibitor approved for severe alopecia areata (autoimmune hair loss), not for ordinary pattern baldness, and carrying a boxed warning.
card.note: Boxed warning for serious infection, clots, cardiovascular events and cancer; evidence applies to alopecia areata only.

quick.overview:
Baricitinib is a once-daily pill that dampens the immune signalling behind alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy to total hair loss. It was FDA-approved for severe cases in adults in 2022.

Two phase 3 trials showed more regrowth than placebo at the higher dose. It is not tested or approved for common pattern baldness.
quick.mechanism: It blocks JAK1 and JAK2 enzymes, which relay inflammatory cytokine signals, reducing the immune attack on hair follicles.
quick.risks: The label carries a boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, cancer, major cardiovascular events and blood clots. Monitoring of blood counts, lipids and liver tests is required.
